children: marginally missed first-quarter sales and profit estimates on Thursday, as budget-conscious diners curtailed restaurant spending and prioritized value-focused purchases.
Shares of the Olive Garden parent were down about 5% in premarket trading, even as the company reaffirmed its annual forecasts.

Consumers became increasingly selective about discretionary purchases this year, as concerns over inflation, gasoline prices and the broader economic outlook continued to shape household spending decisions.

Eating at home remained a lower-cost alternative for many households, limiting the ability of casual-dining chains to lift guest counts even as restaurant operators responded with bundled meals, limited-time offers and menu additions.
The company reported sales of $3.20 billion in the first quarter, compared with analysts' estimate of $3.21 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG.
Its quarterly adjusted profit from continuing operations came in at $2.05 per share, below analysts' average estimate of $2.06.
